analytics_privacy_title: What this dashboard does not know, on purpose
analytics_privacy_noCookies: No cookies, no browser storage, no tracking script and no third party: nothing is installed in a visitor's browser to produce these numbers.
analytics_privacy_noBeacon: The only thing a browser ever sends is a short error report when a page breaks (see Browser errors) — no cookie, nothing stored, no identifier, and nothing under Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track. Page-speed measurements taken in the browser (Web Vitals) would need consent, so speed here is measured on the server only.
analytics_errors_intro: What broke in visitors' browsers, grouped by bug. A report holds the error message, where in our code it happened, the page type, the app version and the browser family — no account, no address, no identifier, and nothing is stored on the visitor's device. Browsers sending Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track send nothing.

analytics_errors_olderNote: Nothing older than {counts} days is kept, so the start of this period is empty.
analytics_errors_none: No browser errors were reported in this period.

analytics_errors_kind_sveltekit: Error while loading or drawing a page
featureFlags_label_clientErrors: Browser error reports (no cookie, no identifier)
analytics_privacy_noIdentifiers: No IP address and no browser string reaches these numbers: they are reduced to a route, a status, a browser family and a day before they are counted.
analytics_privacy_anonymous: Anonymous visitors are not counted as people. No identifier exists to count them by, so they appear only as requests.
analytics_privacy_search: Search terms are never recorded; only that a search happened.
analytics_privacy_small: Groups of fewer than {k} people are shown as “<{k}”, never as a number.
analytics_privacy_objection: Requests from browsers that send Global Privacy Control or Do Not Track are left out of these statistics entirely. They are still written to the security log, which is what spam and abuse are fought with — the objection is to statistics, not to keeping the site safe.
analytics_privacy_minors: Accounts of minors (under 16, or created by a guardian) are not counted in active-account and retention figures.
analytics_privacy_staff: Staff accounts (moderators and administrators) are not counted as people — not in active accounts, retention, registrations or the funnel. Their requests still count as traffic.
analytics_privacy_retention: Aggregates are kept for at most 25 months and then deleted.

account_settingsLink: Your data and deleting your account
account_settingsLinkHint: Download a copy of everything EdMat holds about you, or delete your account.
account_exportBody: One file with everything EdMat holds about you: your profile and settings, what you have written and published, your private messages (decrypted), bookings, registrations, study sets, flashcards, notifications, and the last 90 days of the server's record of your requests. It is a JSON file — readable by programs, and by people with a text editor; every field is described inside it. Other people appear in it only under the name the site showed you, never with their e-mail address.
account_exportDone: Downloaded — the file is in your browser's downloads.
account_exportLimit: You can download it three times a day.
account_exportThrottled: You have downloaded it three times today. Try again tomorrow.
account_deleteIntro: Deleting your account switches it off at once — you are signed out everywhere and your profile is hidden — and erases it for good after {days} days. Until then you can change your mind by signing in again. This is exactly what will happen:
account_action_keep: Kept as a record, without your name
account_action_end: Ended — the other side is told
account_why_delete: Private to you, and nobody else relies on it.
account_why_anonymise: Published for others under the content licence (terms § 9), so people may already rely on it. Your name is replaced by "Deleted account".
account_why_keep: A record other people rely on — a decision, a vote counted in a result, a booking the other side had, a conversation that is also theirs. It says "Deleted account", not your name.
account_why_end: Still under way with somebody else: a future booking is cancelled, a seat at an upcoming event is freed, a course is left. They are told.
account_what_sign_in: Sign-in: password, sessions, linked Google / Apple / Microsoft accounts, e-mail confirmation
account_what_notifications: Notifications and the e-mail digest setting
account_what_history: Which exercises and materials you opened
account_what_follows: Followed tags, watched listings, bookmarks and saved comments
account_what_study: Study sets, flashcard decks and review schedules, course notes and progress
account_what_education: Education profile, diplomas, grades and course certificates
account_what_participation: Course enrolments, event registrations, contest entries and volunteer shifts
account_what_roles: Roles: staff of a course or event, organisation and project membership, task assignments
account_what_contributions: Exercises, solutions, translations, materials, concept articles and pictures
account_what_hosted: Courses, events, contests, organisations, tasks, plans and goals you created
account_what_records: Decisions you made as a reviewer, moderator or organiser
account_what_reports: Reports, notices and bug reports you filed
account_what_terms: Your acceptance of the terms of use
account_what_feed: Your entries in the activity feed
account_what_mail: The log of e-mails we sent you
account_what_request_log: The server's request log (deleted after 90 days in any case)
account_what_audit: The administrative record of what you did (sign-ins, decisions)
account_blockedHeading: First, hand these over or close them
account_blocked_course: a course people are taking part in — finish it, or hand it to another instructor
account_blocked_event: an upcoming event people have registered for — cancel it, or hand it to a co-organiser
account_blocked_contest: a contest that is under way — close or cancel it first
account_blocked_soleOwner: you are its only owner — make somebody else an owner first
account_children: These child accounts have no other guardian, so they will be deleted together with yours:
account_refusal_guardianManaged: Your account is managed by your parent or guardian, so only they can delete it — ask your parent or guardian; they can do it from their own Settings. You can still download your data above.
account_choice_heading: Your published content that is not openly licensed
account_choice_intro: {count} of the things you published are under "EdMat only" (or have no declared licence). You decide what happens to them:
account_choice_keep: Keep them published, under "Deleted account" instead of your name ({count})
account_choice_remove: Remove them ({count}) — they are hidden from everyone; comments and links to them stay, so nobody's thread breaks
account_choice_shared: {count} more have other people's work in them (a co-author's version or revision), so they stay either way. You can still ask us to take a particular one down.
account_choice_open: Content under a Creative Commons licence always stays, without your name: that licence cannot be taken back, and others may already have copies they are allowed to keep. You can still ask us to remove a particular item, and we will unless it has become part of someone else's work.
account_choice_required: Choose first what happens to your "EdMat only" content.
account_refusal_passwordRequired: You sign in only through another service. To confirm a deletion we ask for your password, so set one first under "Sign-in methods" in Settings.
account_error_alreadyPending: A deletion is already waiting for this account.
account_scheduledBody: It will be deleted for good on {date}. Until then you can change your mind: sign in with your password and choose to cancel, or use the link in the e-mail we sent to your confirmed address.
account_loginPending: This account is switched off and will be deleted on {date}.
account_loginCancel: Cancel the deletion and sign in
account_loginGuardian: Your guardian asked for this account to be deleted. Only they can cancel it.
account_cancelDone: The deletion is cancelled and your account is active again. You can sign in.
account_cancelInvalid: This link does not work — it may be incomplete. Sign in with your password instead; you will be asked whether to cancel.
account_cancelNothing: There is no deletion waiting any more: it was already cancelled, or it has been carried out.
licence_suggestOwn: Suggested: CC BY 4.0, because this is your own work, written here. Others may build on it as long as they name you. You can choose differently.
licence_suggestSource: This names a source, so it may be somebody else’s work — not yours to open. It stays “EdMat only” unless you hold the rights and choose otherwise.
licence_suggestNotFromScratch: A file or a link may be somebody else’s work — not yours to open. It stays “EdMat only” unless you hold the rights and choose otherwise. Written here from scratch, it would be suggested as CC BY 4.0.
sso_error_minor: This account is run by a parent or guardian, so an outside account cannot be connected to it. Ask your guardian.
sso_error_passwordWrong: That is not this account's password.
sso_error_tooManyAttempts: Too many wrong passwords for this request. Start again from the sign-in page.
sso_error_methodUnavailable: That way of proving the account is not available for it.
sso_error_linkInvalid: This link has expired, has already been used, or a newer one was sent. Start again from the sign-in page.
sso_error_linkOtherBrowser: Open this link in the same browser where you started signing in. Nothing was connected.
sso_link_intro: This address already has an EdMat account. Prove it is yours to connect {provider} to it — nothing is connected until you do.
sso_link_byEmail: With a link sent to this address
sso_link_emailSent: We sent a link to {email}. Open it in this browser within 30 minutes.
sso_link_notYou: Not your account? Leave this page — nothing will be connected.
course_kind_topicHint: A community around a subject, for everyone learning it wherever they study — e.g. “Linear algebra”. Universities and faculties can then add their own versions under it.
course_kind_universityHint: A course at one university with no general course here yet. If there is one, open it and add a university/faculty version instead.
course_form_universityHint: Its full name, e.g. “University of Warsaw” — other students find the course by it.
course_form_subjectHint: Ties the course to a subject here, so it can say which topics it covers.
course_materialsIndex_empty: No materials have been added to this course yet.
course_materialsIndex_emptyCanAdd: No materials yet — add the first one under “Add something” below.
materials_hub_coursesLink: Courses & communities collect materials for one topic or one university course in one place →
course_version_lead: Your university’s (and faculty’s) own group for this course: its own people, materials and discussion — and its materials also show up on the general course’s page.
course_versions_empty: No university has its own version of this course yet. Studying it somewhere? Add yours — its materials will show up here too.
course_version_refusal_parentNotFound: That general course is not visible to you.
course_version_refusal_parentIsSubcourse: A version cannot have versions of its own — add it under the general course.
course_version_refusal_parentNotGeneral: Versions are added under a general course, not under one university’s course.
course_version_refusal_hasSubcourses: This course already has versions, so it cannot become one.
course_version_refusal_parentIsSelf: A course cannot be a version of itself.
course_version_refusal_parentFixed: A version stays under the general course it was created in.
course_version_refusal_moreVisible: A version cannot be more visible than its general course — pick the same visibility or a narrower one.

empty_orgsAll: This is where faculties, schools and student circles show who they are and what they run. None is listed yet.
empty_orgsMine: Organisations you belong to will be listed here. Someone who runs one can add you, or you can found your own.
empty_concepts: A concept page explains one idea, like a limit or a group, with a separate article for each kind of reader. Nobody has written one yet.

empty_eventsHosting: Events you organise will be listed here.
empty_eventsAttending: When you say you are going to an event, it shows up here.
empty_activityAll: Everything public that happens here, from new exercises and solutions to courses and posts, shows up in this feed. It is quiet so far.
empty_activityFollowed: This view shows only what you follow: tags you watch and courses you have joined. Nothing has come from them yet.
empty_mySet: Your set is a study sheet you put together yourself: add exercises while browsing, then print them with or without hints and solutions.
